correctness.rationale: The proof forces union coverage by embeddings, excludes words of the sum of input lengths by a marker-position uniqueness contradiction, then splits length-sum-minus-one words into one shared zero or one shared one. Complete zero-gap tightness classification proves every necessary and sufficient condition and the binomial counts, including one-symbol boundary cases; complementation yields the second branch. The two embedded standalone programs verified 81 exhaustive quadruples (866 maximal words) and 625 constructive quadruples (130102 outputs). Neither finite test is interpreted as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2026 full text proves general output-delay enumeration of all minimal common supersequences through a unique DAG path characterization, not a symbolic four-run count. The 1996 full article develops a dynamic program to determine the length of a longest minimal common supersequence; an algorithm returning an extremal length does not imply the number of attaining words. These general algorithms can calculate individual cases, but do not furnish the four-parameter classification as an expressed theorem.

value.rationale: The four-run opposite-input family is an elementary but structurally important special case of longest deletion-minimal sequence merging, where knowing the extremal length does not determine the number of extremizers. The theorem classifies a natural entire four-dimensional parameter family with exact binomial factors, a two-type explanation of shared-position ambiguity, and an exceptional combinatorial phase at unit endpoint runs. Previous two-parameter binomial spectra do not settle the independently varied other run lengths.
